top_cited_works.title: XFOIL: An Analysis and Design System for Low Reynolds Number Airfoils
Viscous-inviscid analysis of transonic and low Reynolds number airfoils
top_cited_works.abstract: A method of accurately calculating transonic and low Reynolds number airfoil flows, implemented in the viscous-inviscid design/analysis code ISES, is presented. The Euler equations are discretized on a conservative streamline grid and are strongly coupled to a two-equation integral boundary-layer formulation, using the displacement thickness concept. A transition prediction formulation of the e9 type is derived and incorporated into the viscous formulation. The entire discrete equation set, including the viscous and transition formulations, is solved as a fully coupled nonlinear system by a global Newton method. This is a rapid and reliable method for dealing with strong viscous-inviscid interactions, which invariably occur in transonic and low Reynolds number airfoil flows. The results presented demonstrate the ability of the ISES code to predict transitioning separation bubbles and their associated losses. The rapid airfoil performance degradation with decreasing Reynolds number is thus accurately predicted. top_cited_works.title: Power Balance in Aerodynamic Flows
top_cited_works.abstract: A control volume analysis of the compressible viscous flow about an aircraft is performed,including integrated propulsors and flow control systems. In contrast to most past analyses which have focused on forces and momentum flow, in particular thrust and drag, the present analysis focuses on mechanical power and kinetic energy flow. The result is a clear identification and quantification of all the power sources, power sinks, and their interactions which are present in any aerodynamic flow. The formulation does not require any separate definitions of thrust and drag, and hence it is especially useful for analysis and optimization of aerodynamic configurations which have tightly integrated propulsion and boundary layer control systems.

recent_works.title: Testing of a Ducted-Fan Blown Lift Aircraft Concept
Landing Trajectory Planning for Ultra-STOL Aircraft Subjected to Disturbances
recent_works.abstract: This paper investigates the limits of controllability of ultra Short Takeoff and Landing (uSTOL) aircraft, focusing on precision landing approaches at very low airspeeds. These landings require extremely high lift coefficients enabled by blown lift resulting in highly nonlinear and power-dependent aerodynamic characteristics and flight far on the back side of the power curve. Additionally, the low speeds make uSTOL aircraft highly sensitive to gusts and any control compensation; effects further complicated by the blown-lift aerodynamics. The paper will use nonlinear trajectory optimization to determine the best possible trajectories within physical limits assuming perfect knowledge of the disturbance field. The objective is to inform the design of uSTOL landing control systems which will reduce the dispersion from gusts and other perturbations to acceptable levels.

recent_works.title: PVU: A Medium-Order Finite Element Panel Method
recent_works.abstract: A new type of Panel-Vertex-Unstructured (PVU) method is presented, which combines an established Morino-type source+doublet Dirichlet formulation with modern finite-element solution techniques for completely arbitrary unstructured meshes. The discretization uses nodal variables and bilinear interpolation over elements, and a Galerkin weighted-residual integration is used to construct the discrete residuals at the nodes, thus allowing any unstructured mix of triangular and quadrilateral elements. Numerical differentiation for the surface velocity and pressure calculation also uses a finite element weighted-residual approach, and is also applicable to any unstructured mesh topology. Compressibility is handled by a standard Prandtl-Glauert treatment. A two-layer wake formulation enables evaluation of wake velocities with the finite-element based method, simplifying strong boundary layer coupling. The two-layer wake also simplifies propulsor jet modeling. In lieu of the constant-strength ``wake strip'' structured-mesh treatment of traditional panel methods, the wake zero pressure jump convective equation is solved on the wake using a Petrov-Galerkin weighted residual discretization....

recent_works.title: TASOPT.jl: A Julia package for conceptual commercial transport aircraft design
recent_works.venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
